findings.body: When the app-server identity lookup fails, `identity()` returns only its PID. This code persists that incomplete identity and still acknowledges it, allowing the driver to start a conversation without recording the required start time and command. If the driver subsequently dies, `_stop_leftover()` cannot recover that server because its record lacks a command. Require a complete identity before acknowledging startup; otherwise stop the owned driver group and refuse. Add coverage where only the app-server identity lookup fails.
findings.title: Not done: 5. Record the complete process identity before any conversation

findings.body: An unreadable leftover identity makes `_alive()` return `None`, which this condition silently skips. After a crash with a dead Forge owner and an unidentifiable surviving app-server, `hold()` therefore permits another worker. `run()` then overwrites the old process identities at line 163, permanently losing the information needed to clean up the survivor. Doctor also silently skips this unresolved process. Distinguish an unknown identity from a confirmed absent or mismatched process, preserve its record, and refuse new work until cleanup can be verified.
findings.title: Not done: 6. Preserve unresolved leftovers before starting another worker
